Facility Description (Stationary Source)
Name: Emerald Kalama Chemical, LLC
Address: 1296 Third Street NW,  Kalama, WA  98625-9799
EPA ID#: WAD092899574

This Risk Management Plan (RMP) submittal outlines the facilitys comprehensive approach to managing chemical process risks in accordance with the requirements of 40 CFR Part 68, as mandated by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). The purpose of this plan is to ensure the safety of employees, the surrounding community, and the environment through proactive risk identification, mitigation, and emergency preparedness.

We at Lanxess Corporation are strongly committed to employee, public, and environmental safety. This commitment is inherent to a comprehensive accidental release prevention program in place that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training associated with the processes at our facility. It is our policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances

Facility Description & RMP Applicability
The Facility, located at 1296 Third Street NW, Kalama, WA 98625, is on the north boundary of the city of Kalama, Washington 0.25 miles west of the US Interstate 5. The Facility sits on the Columbia River at river mile post 74. The Sites footprint is 155 acres, with approximately 44 acres occupied. 
The Facility operates 24 hours a day, 365 days per year. The site manages acetaldehyde above its threshold quantity of 10,000 lbs, therefore the process it is used in requires a Risk Management Plan (RMP).  Acetaldehyde is used to manufacture flavor and/or fragrance products. This process is also an OSHA Process Safety Management (PSM)-covered and is a RMP Program Level III process under the scope of the Risk Management Plan. 

Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response 
Acetaldehyde is stored on site in a storage tank and in one or two rail cars. The maximum intended inventory of acetaldehyde on site is con

trolled by administrative procedures and storage capacity. 
The modeled Worst-Case Release scenario would result in an off-site impact. Administrative controls and technical mitigation measures such as passive temperature monitoring and deluge system, operating procedures, and an emergency response plan are in place to limit the impact distance and severity. Alternative release scenarios were assessed in the Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) in accordance with PSM regulations. 

The facility has an emergency response plan designed to respond to and mitigate the release scenarios identified in the PHA. The facility maintains an on-site Emergency Response Team that is organized and trained according to the National Incident Command System, ensuring seamless integration with external agencies. The plan has been reviewed and modified as necessary to coordinate with the community's emergency response plan. 

Five Year Accident History
There have been no release events involving acetaldehyde meeting the 5-year accidental release criteria at the facility in the RMP reporting history. 

General Accidental Release Prevention and Risk Management Program 
The facility complies with applicable RMP regulations and is committed to continuous improvement in process safety. Regular audits, incident investigations, and community outreach are integral to our risk management strategy. This submittal provides assurance to regulators and stakeholders of our ongoing efforts to prevent accidents and protect public health and the environment. The facility manages its risk by implementing PSM elements that are aligned with those in the EPA Risk Management Plan. The PSM Elements are:

Employee Participation  Employees participate in safety committees that potentially affect the work life of each area at the Kalama facility. Action items that are identified from inspections, incidents, process hazards analyses, etc. are provided to employees for review.

Process Safety Information  All site per

sonnel have access to the company's electronic mail system and Intranet. Chemical-specific information (Safety Data Sheets), operating information, and information on the equipment in the process are easily accessible. The information resides in a controlled electronic system that is updated regularly. All Process Safety Information (PSI) is verified at each scheduled process hazards analysis.

Process Hazard Analysis  Every five years, process hazards analyses (PHAs) are conducted in each process. The Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) method is used. Findings are identified, prioritized and then promptly corrected. The information is shared with personnel who are impacted by the findings. The action items and completion schedules are managed in an electronic system.
Operating Procedures  Procedures that address normal and abnormal operating situations are in place. The procedures are reviewed annually to ensure accuracy.

Training  Training is ongoing to ensure that operators know and understand the safe operation of their unit and that they understand the necessary actions for abnormal situations. Employee training is documented and tracked through a network system. The system allows specific training needs to be identified as well as tracks the completion of required modules.

Contractor Safety  Control of contractor activity in operating areas is well established. Contract employees are required to participate annually in comprehensive industry safety training. On occasion, the company hires contractors to conduct specialized maintenance and construction activities. Prior to selecting a contractor, a thorough evaluation of safety performance of the contractor is carried out. Contractors are informed of procedures for emergency response should an accidental release of a regulated substance occur. When contractor employees are brought on site before starting work, they are required to watch the "Contractor Safety" video and annually thereafter.

Pre-Startup Safet

y Reviews  Pre-start up safety reviews related to new processes and to modifications in established processes are conducted. These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment, operating and maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation. Findings are addressed prior to startup.
Mechanical Integrity  Mechanical integrity procedures are in place to ensure that maintenance workers understand how to perform their duties safely to maintain the facility. Specific instructions for testing and inspections are included. Testing and inspections are conducted as scheduled and documented. Maintenance and engineering follow established codes, standards and company guidelines.

Hot Work and Control of Abnormal Activities  Control of hot work and abnormal situations is conducted via the permitting and temporary management of change process to ensure that work does not contribute to or cause hazardous results. All aspects of hot work and abnormal situations are controlled.

Management of Change  Written procedures are in place at the Kalama Plant to manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment and procedures. Process operators, maintenance personnel or any other employee whose job tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are promptly made aware of and offered training by area supervision to deal with the modification.

Incident Investigations  Incidents, injuries and near-miss situations are investigated. Root causes are identified and documented. Changes in the system are made to prevent recurrence. Incident reports are readily available to assist other areas in preventing similar occurrences.
Compliance Audits  A site-wide compliance audit is conducted every three years of the PSM-RMP program. Deficiencies are documented and corrected in a timely manner. Open action items are tracked through completion.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety 
The LANXESS Kalama facility practices c

ontinual improvement. Periodic PHAs and Facility Siting reviews provide a mechanism for assessing and improving process safety and risk management. The plant is planning several upgrades to process equipment in the next few years.
